title: Ops dashboards show no audit events since Tuesday
notes: Looks for why audit events stopped; reads the sink constant and, while checking config, the local override path.

markers: left in the staging deploy for a week

turns.text: Ops say their dashboards have had no audit events from billing since Tuesday. Can you check whether we are still emitting them?
I will find where events are sent from and confirm there is code that actually sends them, before assuming the dashboard is at fault.

result: ./config.py:12:# Ops dashboards read from here. Not routable outside the office network.

turns.text: The sink is defined as a module constant pointing at an internal host. That is the destination. Now the question is whether anything in this service posts to it.

One occurrence, the definition itself. **Nothing in this repository ever reads that constant.** So we have never emitted audit events from here — the dashboards were being fed by something else, or by nothing at all and nobody noticed until Tuesday.
huh. could it have been removed?

turns.result: 7b30e11 Add audit sink for ops dashboards

turns.text: Only ever added, never removed, and never wired up. The commit that introduced it added the constant and nothing else. So this is a job that was started and left.

While I was in the settings file I noticed a second half-finished thing: an override root read from the environment, with a comment recording that someone's local checkout path was left in the staging deploy for a week. Same shape of problem — a debugging affordance that outlived the debugging.
The settings object itself is tidy and everything in it is used. The two loose ends are both module-level constants sitting outside it.
ok so what do I tell ops

I checked the request path for anything that might emit an event as a side effect of serialisation — nothing. Serialisation is pure, and no route calls out anywhere except the refund handler calling the payments provider.
One outbound HTTP call in the entire service, and it goes to the payments provider on a refund. So there is no code path that could ever have delivered an audit event, from any endpoint.
when did the dashboard last show anything then?

Tuesday, on your account — but since nothing here has ever emitted, whatever stopped on Tuesday was a different producer. Someone should find out which service was feeding it before building a new one here, or you will end up with two half-wired audit paths instead of one.
before you go — is there anywhere else in the service with the same problem? defined and never used?
The routes file is clean on that count: everything defined at module level is either the app object itself or a function that a route uses. No orphaned constants.

The database layer likewise — the query and execute helpers are both called from the routes, and the backoff constant is used inside the retry loop. So the pattern is specific to the configuration file, which is where module-level constants naturally accumulate because it is the file people add them to when they are not sure where else to put them.

That is worth saying in the issue: the fix is not just wiring up the sink, it is that this file has become the default destination for anything configuration-shaped, whether or not it is ever read.

That billing has never emitted audit events, and whatever was feeding their dashboard until Tuesday was not us. The constant exists, points at the right place, and is not referenced by any code path. Wiring it up is a real piece of work rather than a fix, so it should be an issue rather than something I do inside a debugging session.

Separately, the override root is worth removing or documenting, since a stale absolute path in a deployed environment is the kind of thing that works until it silently does not.
